# ThanosFx

ThanosFx is a zero-dependency WebGL2 library that burns and reassembles real DOM elements. It captures the element as a texture, renders a full-screen overlay, and animates the element with GPU particles. The underlying DOM is left untouched until the effect finishes.

Use it for delete/recycle transitions, destructive actions, and assemble/reveal moments.

## Requirements

- A browser with WebGL2.
- Client-side JavaScript or TypeScript.
- The target must be an `HTMLElement` attached to the document and visible when the effect starts.
- Wait for images and fonts to load before capturing if they are part of the element.
- The library is DOM-only. It does not render to canvas/WebGL scenes.

## Install

```sh
npm install thanosfx
```

React is optional and only needed for the `thanosfx/react` entry point:

```sh
npm install react
```

## Import

```ts
import { assemble, burn, createEffect, effectNames, playEffect } from "thanosfx";
import type {
  AttractorLike,
  EffectHandle,
  EffectName,
  EffectOptions,
  RectLike,
} from "thanosfx";
```

## API

### `burn(target, options?)`

Burns the element into dust.

```ts
const handle = burn(card, {
  duration: 1700,
  attractTo: bin,
  attractStrength: 0.9,
  attractSwirl: 0.3,
  collision: false,
});
```

### `assemble(target, options?)`

Burn played backwards. Dust gathers and the element appears.

```ts
assemble(card, {
  duration: 1800,
  attractTo: addButton,
  removeTarget: false,
});
```

### `playEffect(target, effect, options?)`

Starts an effect by name: `"burn"` or `"assemble"`.

```ts
playEffect(card, "burn", { duration: 1200 });
```

### `createEffect(target, effect, options?)`

Generic form of `playEffect`.

```ts
createEffect(card, "assemble", { removeTarget: false });
```

### `effectNames`

`["burn", "assemble"]`

### `EffectHandle`

Every call returns an `EffectHandle`:

```ts
interface EffectHandle {
  readonly promise: Promise<void>;
  cancel(): void;
}
```

- `promise` resolves when the effect finishes or is cancelled.
- `cancel()` stops the animation and restores the target.

## Options

```ts
interface EffectOptions {
  duration?: number; // milliseconds
  removeTarget?: boolean; // burn defaults to true, assemble to false
  dpr?: number; // device pixel ratio override
  reducedMotion?: "auto" | "allow" | "reduce";
  burnMs?: number;
  density?: number;
  gravity?: number;
  bounce?: number;
  spread?: number;
  life?: number;
  friction?: number;
  lift?: number;
  particleScale?: number;
  embers?: boolean;
  collision?: boolean;
  mode?: "sweep" | "instant";
  collideWith?: RectLike[];
  attractTo?: AttractorLike | null;
  attractStrength?: number; // 0–1
  attractSwirl?: number; // negative reverses the curl
}
```

Library defaults:

| Option             | Default                 |
| ------------------ | ----------------------- |
| `duration`         | `1700` burn, `1800` assemble |
| `removeTarget`     | `true` burn, `false` assemble |
| `dpr`              | automatic, capped at 2  |
| `reducedMotion`    | `"auto"`                |
| `burnMs`           | `200`                   |
| `density`          | `0.9`                   |
| `gravity`          | `3200`                  |
| `bounce`           | `0.32`                  |
| `spread`           | `210`                   |
| `life`             | `1`                     |
| `friction`         | `0.66`                  |
| `lift`             | `190`                   |
| `particleScale`    | `1`                     |
| `embers`           | `true`                  |
| `collision`        | `true`                  |
| `mode`             | `"sweep"`               |
| `collideWith`      | `[]`                    |
| `attractTo`        | `null`                  |
| `attractStrength`  | `0.7`                   |
| `attractSwirl`     | `0.35`                  |

## Particle modes

### Collision

Dust bounces off the listed elements or rects.

```ts
const cards = [...document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(".task")];
const card = cards[0];
if (!card) throw new Error("Missing task");

await burn(card, {
  collision: true,
  collideWith: cards.filter((element) => element !== card),
}).promise;
```

### Attract

Dust spirals into an element, rect, or point.

```ts
const bin = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(".recycle-bin")!;

await burn(card, {
  attractTo: bin,
  attractStrength: 0.9,
  attractSwirl: 0.3,
  collision: false,
}).promise;
```

`attractTo` accepts:

- an `Element`
- a `DOMRect`
- `{ left, top, width, height }`
- `[x, y, width, height]`
- `{ x, y }`
- `[x, y]`

### Dissolve

No collision and no attractor. Dust falls and drifts away.

```ts
await burn(card, {
  collision: false,
  gravity: 450,
  spread: 240,
  lift: 210,
}).promise;
```

## Recommended cleanup pattern

For delete/recycle flows, keep the element in the layout until the effect finishes:

```ts
const card = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(".task")!;
const bin = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(".recycle-bin")!;

const handle = burn(card, {
  attractTo: bin,
  collision: false,
  removeTarget: false,
});

await handle.promise;
card.remove();
```

`removeTarget: false` prevents the library from removing the element before your layout logic runs. If a row should keep its space reserved during the effect, leave it in place and remove it after the promise resolves.

For assemble flows, keep `removeTarget: false` so the element remains visible after the dust gathers.

## React

```tsx
import { useRef } from "react";
import { useThanosFx } from "thanosfx/react";

export function DeleteCard() {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const { play, cancel } = useThanosFx(ref, "burn", {
    attractTo: document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(".recycle-bin"),
    collision: false,
    removeTarget: false,
  });

  return (
    <div ref={ref}>
      <button onClick={() => void play()?.promise.then(() => ref.current?.remove())}>
        Delete
      </button>
      <button onClick={cancel}>Cancel</button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`useThanosFx(ref, effect, options)` returns:

```ts
{
  play(): EffectHandle | null;
  cancel(): void;
}
```

The `ThanosFx` component is also available:

```tsx
import { ThanosFx } from "thanosfx/react";

<ThanosFx effect="burn" options={{ duration: 1700 }} autoPlay>
  <div className="card">Delete me</div>
</ThanosFx>;
```

## Reduced motion and WebGL2

- `reducedMotion: "auto"` honors `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- `"reduce"` forces the short opacity fallback.
- `"allow"` forces the full particle effect.
- If WebGL2 is unavailable, the effect cannot run. Let the promise reject or fall back to your own fade.

## Troubleshooting

**Nothing happens**

- Check that the target is an `HTMLElement` in the document.
- Check that the target has a non-zero size.
- Check that WebGL2 is available.
- Make sure the element is not `display: none` or `visibility: hidden`.

**Images are missing from the effect**

- Wait for images to decode before starting.
- Cross-origin images can prevent canvas capture. Use same-origin images or data URLs.
- If an optional global `html2canvas` is present, ThanosFx uses it; otherwise it uses an SVG `foreignObject` snapshot.

**The layout jumps**

- Use `removeTarget: false`.
- Keep the element in place until `handle.promise` resolves.
- Remove the element yourself after the effect.

**The target disappears immediately**

- Check the `removeTarget` option.
- Check whether `cancel()` was called.
